description:
Scenario: MemoryBackend::with_account('').register_account(&Id::from('')) creates an account whose id is the empty string. Later AddressBook/get { accountId: '' } succeeds against it.

Bad behavior consequence: the empty-string-as-Id is at best confusing in test output and at worst a maintenance hazard if a contributor copy-pastes the with_account('') invocation. Id::from is infallible by design (the workspace newtype), so the validation gap is in the higher-level helper.

The same gap exists in seed_object — no validation on the type_name string, no validation on the id string. A typo seed_object('acc1', 'AddreesBook', ...) creates a phantom HashMap slot under ('AddreesBook', 'acc1') that no read path will ever find.

Suggested rewrite: at minimum, add debug_assert!(!account_id.is_empty(), ...) and debug_assert!(matches!(type_name, 'AddressBook' | 'ContactCard'), ...) to with_account / register_account / seed_object. This is a demo backend, so the cost is zero in release and the developer-experience gain in tests is positive. A typoed type_name would fail loudly in debug.

Lower-priority because the surface area is internal (test fixtures) and the failure mode is 'fixture didn't load, test still passes vacuously', which is a tractable observable failure. Still worth a defensive assert.
title: register_account accepts empty-string accountId silently — Id::from('') yields a usable but invalid account
